headline: Anthropic told an Australian parliamentary inquiry that the country's current copyright law makes it impossible to train AI models there.
score_reason: New, on the record at a hearing, with creators' groups giving opposing evidence.
importance_line: Australian writers, musicians and artists could see their work opened to AI training if the rules loosen, and AI firms say they cannot train locally under the current law, but no law change has been made.
summary: The Sydney Morning Herald reports that Jeff Bleich, Anthropic's special envoy and a former US ambassador to Australia, told a parliamentary committee in Sydney on 6 Oct 2026 that it is technically impossible to "license the entire internet" and that training in Australia could be found illegal without a licence from every rights holder; Journal Arta adds he said Anthropic had "never tried to dictate to Australia". Groups for about 128,000 songwriters and over 40,000 authors and artists told the same inquiry that AI companies must pay to train on Australian work, while lawmakers weigh whether rights holders should have to opt out.
notes: Books+Publishing (pool source) relays another outlet; SMH is the original hearing report. The SMH URL slug does not match the headline but the page text is the hearing report.
